metadata.title: When Pedal Shapes Come Back: a Complex Story
metadata.abstract: Under the usual nondegeneracy assumptions, repeatedly projecting a fixed point onto the side lines of an $n$-gon returns its shape after $n$ steps. We explain this classical theorem through a short complex-number identity: the multipliers of one step move cyclically around the polygon. The same calculation allows a different common angle of projection at each step. A sharp angle-dependent contraction bound identifies the incircle centre as the maximiser for tangential polygons. In space, even a regular tetrahedron can fail to recover its shape after four steps. We give an exact example, then show how concentric inscribed and circumscribed spheres restore a two-step return. Rectangular boxes provide a further four-step family.

analysis.workSummary: 在通常非退化条件下，对固定点反复向n边形边所在直线投影，n步后恢复原形状；作者用一步乘子的循环复数恒等式解释经典结论，并允许每步不同共同投影角。另给尖锐角依赖收缩界，切多边形以内心为极大者。
techniques: 三维形状回归及球面条件
analysis.breakthrough: 三维给正四面体四步不回归的精确例子，并说明同心内外接球可恢复两步回归，长方体还有四步族。
analysis.limitations: 平面经典定理的新解释不等于任意退化多边形或三维多面体普遍回归；形状回归是相似意义而非逐点位置不变。 当前数学解读依据摘要，尚未逐步审读证明。
